predecessors.note: Cliopatria's East Franks row (850-910) draws Franconia as the core of East Francia; 'Henry, titled Margrave of the Franks' held the region 882-92 and Conrad the Younger is mentioned as dux Franconiae in 906 (Duchy of Franconia page).

land.text: the Main valley from the Rhine to the Nordgau, with the left-bank Gaue around Mainz, Speyer and Worms; Hesse (Hessengau, Lahngau) to the north

successors.note: After the Battle of Andernach on 2 October 939 Otto I seized the duchy, appointed no new duke and let it split into counties and bishoprics answering directly to the king; Eberhard's page has it a direct imperial possession until 1039. The ducal title went to the Bishopric of Würzburg in 1168 (Duchy of Franconia page).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Franconia row; its East Franks 850-910 and Kingdom of Germany 911-961 rows draw all Germany as one). The page defines the duchy as the Main valley from its confluence with the Upper Rhine to the Nordgau March, including the Rhine's left-bank Gaue around Mainz, Speyer and Worms, bordering Saxony, Lorraine, Swabia and Bavaria. The infobox gives 906-1168 and no area; the gazetteer shape is about 69,000 km2. The stem duchy proper ends in 939, when Otto I seized it; the 'Duchy of Würzburg' of 1168 is a different, ecclesiastical lordship over East Franconia.

region.text: the Main valley from the Rhine to the Nordgau, with the left-bank Gaue around Mainz, Speyer and Worms; Hesse (Hessengau, Lahngau) to the north

ledger.note: 906: Conrad the Younger is mentioned as dux Franconiae and the infobox dates the duchy's foundation. 'In 906 the Conradine relative Count Conrad the Younger in the Lahngau is mentioned as a dux Franconiae.' Conrad was elected German king in 911 and kept Franconia until his death in 918.

918: Eberhard succeeds his brother Conrad I as duke of Franconia in December 918, after the king's death; in 919 the Saxon Henry the Fowler succeeded Conrad as king. Henry gave Eberhard the regency of Lotharingia in 926 until he enfeoffed Gilbert in 928.

region.text: the Main valley from the Rhine to the Nordgau, with the left-bank Gaue around Mainz, Speyer and Worms; Hesse (Hessengau, Lahngau) to the north

ledger.note: 938: Duke Eberhard rebels against Otto I. 'a rebellion in 938 with Otto's half-brother Thankmar'; he had besieged Helmern Castle in 937 and was fined at Magdeburg. A second revolt in 939 joined Gilbert of Lorraine, Archbishop Frederick of Mainz and Henry, Otto's brother.

region.text: the Main valley from the Rhine to the Nordgau, with the left-bank Gaue around Mainz, Speyer and Worms; Hesse (Hessengau, Lahngau) to the north

ledger.note: 939: the rebels are defeated at Andernach. 'on 2 October 939, the rebels were finally defeated in the Battle of Andernach'; Eberhard was killed there, allegedly by Odo of Wetterau.

region.text: the Main valley from the Rhine to the Nordgau, with the left-bank Gaue around Mainz, Speyer and Worms; Hesse (Hessengau, Lahngau) to the north

ledger.note: 939: Otto I seizes Franconia and appoints no new duke. 'Otto I seized the Franconian stem duchy' after Eberhard's revolt failed at Andernach, and the duchy 'split into counties and bishoprics that answered directly to the king'; Eberhard's page: it 'remained a direct Imperial possession until its dissolution in 1039'.

notes: Two pages opened (budget 2). The stem duchy is short and thinly sourced: no capital is given on either page, so identity.capitals is empty; the extent is the Duchy of Franconia page's description turned into gazetteer regions (Franconia region, Hesse, Mainz-Speyer-Worms circles), confidence 1-2. Not drawn: the Salian lands of Rhenish Franconia (Conrad II became Germany's king in 1024; the page says Rhenish Franconia was governed as small states after 1039; Henry of Laach received the Salian territories in Rhenish Franconia as a fief in 1093, the later Electoral Palatinate) and the Bishopric of Würzburg's 'Duchy of Franconia' of 1168. Eberhard was regent of Lotharingia 926-928; that is not a Franconian gain. Gap: whether 939-1039 should be a 'direct imperial possession' shape of its own.
